04-124.r: Aryadeva → Buddhist philosopher (Nagarjuna's disciple), not Jaina; Dignaga → Buddhist scholar; Nathamuni → first teacher of the Vaishnava sect → only two pairs correct.

04-125.r: Buddhist centre of learning → Vikramshila; others: Nalanda and Vallabhi (drew students from China, Japan, Tibet).

04-126.r: Not a Buddhist learning centre of ancient India → Nagpur. Centres: Vallabhi, Vikramshila, Nalanda.

04-127.r: Vallabhi (Vallabhipura) university → Gujarat; capital of the Maitraka dynasty.

04-128.r: Nalanda (Magadha, Bihar) → founded and flourished under the Gupta dynasty; famous for Buddhist religious philosophy.

04-129.r: Nalanda University → founded by Kumaragupta (Gupta) about 450 AD; called the world's first international university.

04-130.r: Not a Nalanda Acharya → Kautilya (4th-3rd century BCE; Mauryan PM; Arthashastra; linked with Takshashila). Nalanda Acharyas: Nagarjuna, Sheelbhadra, Shantirakshit.

04-132.r: Nalanda lost its glory by the end of the twelfth century: state protection ceased as Palas favoured Vikramshila; Muslim invasion → A and R true, R explains A.

04-133.r: Nava Nalanda Mahavihara → modern Pali and Buddhist research centre; foundation stone laid 20 November 1951.

04-134.r: Common to Buddhism and Jainism → indifference to Vedas, denial of rituals' efficacy, non-injury to animals. Not common → avoiding extremes of penance (Buddhist only; Jains practised self-mortification).

04-137.r: Four Noble Truths in order → suffering; cause of suffering; cessation of suffering; path to cessation (A-D-B-C); first preached at Rishipattan (Sarnath).
04-137.h: Doctor's order: disease, cause, cure exists, medicine.

04-138.r: Jainism and Buddhism both believe in karma and transmigration of soul (rebirth): past actions shape present and future life.

04-139.r: Buddhism accepted rebirth and karma but rejected an immortal soul → A ('rejected rebirth') false, R ('soul is mortal') true.

04-140.r: Buddhism partly accepted caste, challenged the top rank of Brahmins, and placed certain castes as low → all three statements correct.

04-141.r: Spread of Buddhism → simple religion, appeal to Dalits (no caste distinction), missionary spirit, people's language → 1, 2, 3, 4 (not 'Vedic spirit').

04-142.r: Decline of Buddhism (early medieval) → Buddha absorbed into Vaishnavism as an incarnation of Vishnu. Gupta kings were not anti-Buddhist → only statement 1.

04-143.r: Sautrantika and Sammitiya → Buddhist sects, not Jain. Sarvastivada ('all exists') → phenomena not wholly momentary, exist in latent form → only 2 correct.

04-144.r: Chaitya → place of worship (prayer/assembly hall); Vihara → dwelling of monks (rainy-season shelter).
04-144.h: Vihara = where monks reside; Chaitya = where they pray.

04-145.r: Stupa, Chaitya, Vihara → Buddhism. Stupa → burial mound with Buddha's ashes; Chaitya → place of worship; Vihara → monks' dwelling.

04-147.r: Guntuphalli (West Godavari, now NTR district, A.P.) → rock-cut Chaityas and Viharas; Eastern Deccan ones usually rock-cut → both correct.

04-148.r: Stupa → 'to pile up', a structure raised by accumulation; building stupas for the dead existed before Buddhism → both statements true.

04-149.r: Dhanyakataka (now Dharnikota, Palnadu district, Andhra Pradesh) → Mahasanghika Buddhist centre; capital of the later Satavahanas.

04-150.r: Buddhism prominent in the Sultanate period → Vajrayana (flourished from 8th century A.D.); texts: 'Arya Manjushrimulakalpa', 'Guhyasamaja'.

04-151.r: Sanghabhuti (Indian monk, went to China at the end of the fourth century AD) → commentary on the Sarvastivada Vinaya.

05-001.r: Founder of Jainism → Rishabhdev (Adinath), first Tirthankara; Mahavira → 24th Tirthankara (6th century B.C.).

05-003.r: Parshvanath (23rd Tirthankara) → born at Varanasi to King Aswasena and Queen Vama; Kaivalya near Varanasi; Parinirvana at Sammed Shikhar.

05-004.r: Tirthankara symbols: Adinatha → bull; Mallinatha → water jar; Parshvanatha → snake; Sambhavnatha → horse.

05-005.r: Tirthankara symbols: Parshvanath → snake; Adinath → bull; Mahavira → lion; Shantinath → deer.

05-006.r: Wrong pair: Vasupujya (12th Tirthankara) attained Nirvana at Champapur (Bihar), not Sammedashikhar. Correct: Rishabhanath-Ashtapad, Neminath-Urjayanta, Mahavira-Pavapuri.

05-007.r: Shravasti → Sambhavnath; Kakandi → Suvidhinath (Pushpadant); Ayodhya → Rishabhanath; Pabhosa → Padmaprabhu.

05-008.r: Tirthankara order → Abhinandan (4th), Padmaprabhu (6th), Vimal Nath (13th), Munisuvrata Nath (20th).

05-009.r: Mahavira → born at Kundagram (Kundalpur) near Vaishali, about 599 BC; mother Trishala (sister of Lichchhavi chief Chetak); father Siddhartha (Gyatrik Kshatriya).

05-011.r: Mahavira's Nirvana → Pavapuri near Rajgriha, 527 BC, aged about 72; born at Kundagram near Vaishali, 599 BC.

05-013.r: Not true: 'Mahavira never married' – his wife was Yashoda. True: 24th and last Tirthankara; mother was sister of Licchavi Chetaka; died 527 BCE at Pavapuri.

05-014.r: Tirthankara → Jain term; 24 Tirthankaras from Rishabhnath (first) to Mahavira (last); Nathamuni was not a Tirthankara.

05-017.r: Prabhasgiri (Kaushambi, U.P.) → Jain pilgrimage site linked to the 6th Tirthankara, Padmaprabha.

05-018.r: Jain word for complete knowledge → Kaivalya; Mahavira got it after 12 years of austerity, under a Sal tree on the Rijupalika near Jrimbhik; hence 'Kevlin'.

05-019.r: Mahavira's enlightenment → bank of the Rijupalika river, Jrimbhik village.

05-020.r: Three jewels (Triratna) of Jainism → right faith, right knowledge, right action; the means to Moksha.

05-022.r: Triratna → in both Buddhism (Buddha, Dhamma, Sangha) and Jainism (Samyag darshana, Samyag jnana, Samyag charitra).
05-022.c: No answer printed; Triratna fits both Buddhism and Jainism.

05-023.r: Anuvrata (lesser vows for lay people) → Jainism; monks take five Mahavratas: Ahimsa, Satya, Brahmacharya, Asteya, Aparigraha.

05-024.r: Syadvada (knowledge is relative; also Saptabhanginaya) → Jainism, Mahavira's middle path.

05-026.r: Jain doctrines → Anekantavada and Syadvada; Buddhist doctrines → Sunyavada and Sarvastivada.
05-026.t: Sunyavada and Sarvastivada are Buddhist, not Jain.

05-027.r: Jain view: world created and maintained by universal law; universe eternal, without beginning or end; no almighty creator needed.

05-028.r: Anekantavada → core metaphysical theory of Jainism.

05-029.r: Jain philosophy rests on Anekantavada and Syadvada; every being has many properties: permanent = attribute (guna), accidental = mode (paryaya) → both correct.

05-030.r: Jain Tattva (reality) → origination, decay and permanence → all of the above.

05-031.r: Religion with no 'final annihilation of the world' → Jainism (universe and its substances are eternal).

05-032.r: Basic point of Jainism → non-violence (Ahimsa); cardinal principles: Ahimsa, Anekantavada, Aparigraha.

05-033.r: Yapaniya → Jain sect from the Digambaras that also followed some Shwetambara views; worshipped nude Tirthankara images.

05-034.r: Sthanakvasi → Shwetambara Jain sect, from Lonkasha's 'Lonka' sect; holds idol worship not essential for Nirvana.

05-035.r: Earliest Jain holy texts → Fourteen Purvas (preached by all Tirthankaras); Sambhutavijay and Bhadrabahu were the last to know them.

05-036.r: Earliest Jain literature (twelve Angas) → Ardha-Magadhi; finally compiled in the sixth century A.D. at Vallabhi (Gujarat).

05-037.r: Pilgrimage linked to Parshvanath → Sammed Shikhar (his Parinirvana); 23rd Tirthankara, born at Varanasi (850 BC per book), Ikshvaku dynasty.

05-038.r: Not early Jain literature → Therigatha (Buddhist songs of early nuns). Jain texts: Acarangasutra, Sutrakritanga, Brihatkalpasutra.

05-039.r: First leader of the Shwetambaras (first Jain split) → Sthulabhadra; split followed a 12-year famine in Magadha while Bhadrabahu headed the order.

05-040.r: First disciple of Mahavira → Jamali, his son-in-law.

05-042.r: Book: Svetambara Agamas edited at the first Jain Council, Pataliputra, under Chandragupta Maurya.
05-042.c: Question says 'finally edited'; the book elsewhere says Jain texts were finally compiled at Vallabhi (sixth century A.D.); explanation is muddled.

05-044.r: Shvetambara canon includes 12 Angas (true). Book: Angas compiled at the first council at Pataliputra (about 310 BC), not Vallabhi → I true, II false.
05-044.c: The book elsewhere says the Jain canon was finally compiled at Vallabhi (sixth century A.D.), so statement II may be true.
